bullets.title: Anthropic Government Crackdown: AI Export Controls Signal New Regulatory Layer
bullets.body: Anthropic was forced to block foreign access to Fable 5 and Mythos 5 following U.S. national security orders, with Amazon CEO Andy Jassy's talks with Trump administration officials cited as the trigger. Fintwit is split: some see it as bearish TAM compression for frontier AI labs, others argue it accelerates sovereign AI buildouts globally and is net bullish for the broader AI infrastructure trade. A contrarian take: 'The accelerated sovereign AI buildouts globally' offset any TAM collapse, per one analyst.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler Leverage Doubling Every 6 Months—$570B Capex Bond Machine in Motion
bullets.body: Hyperscaler leverage jumped from 0.9x to 1.8x in six months and is rising at 0.3x per quarter, with $570B+ in bond issuance expected in 2026. AMZN issued its largest-ever Canadian bond, GOOGL its biggest-ever JPY bond, and the five largest AI hyperscalers issued 47% more debt in 5 months of 2026 than all of 2024. Credit spreads have drifted from AA to A-level; BBB trajectory flagged within one year.

bullets.title: ORCL Reports $67B Q4 AI Contract Backlog, Warns of $40B Raise—Shares Crater 11%
bullets.body: Oracle signed $67B of AI infrastructure contracts in Q4 and guided FY27 capex to $90-95B (net $70B cash). The company plans to raise ~$40B in debt and equity in FY27 and free cash flow was negative $23.7B in FY26. Stock fell 11%+ and analysts flagged: 'Another trillion gone.' HSBC cut PT to $316 from $345.

bullets.title: NVDA: CPO Timeline Controversy—SemiAnalysis vs. FundaAI vs. Lumentum CEO
bullets.body: SemiAnalysis published a Computex note suggesting 800V DC and CPO scale-up pushed to 2028+, sparking a major intraday selloff in optical/semiconductor names. NVDA's Networking SVP denied delays, Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston confirmed CPO on track and said the NPO opportunity 'is frankly bigger than CPO,' and NVDA stock has denied the 800V DC delay per Morgan Stanley checks. The market appeared to use the report as an excuse to unwind crowded positions.

bullets.title: Meta Forced to Open WhatsApp to Rival AI Chatbots—EU Regulatory Headwind Intensifies
bullets.body: EU antitrust regulators ordered Meta to grant rival AI chatbots unrestricted access to WhatsApp at no charge within 5 days. Meta called the order 'excessive regulation funded by European companies' and announced it will challenge the directive. Separately, Meta's partnership with Manus was unwound after Chinese regulators ordered the deal terminated.

bullets.title: TSLA: Tesla FSD Approved in Denmark; Jensen Huang Endorses QCOM
bullets.body: Tesla's FSD Supervised gained regulatory approval in Denmark. NVDA CEO Jensen Huang separately told investors to 'buy' Qualcomm stock at an event in Seoul, where his visit was described as a 'national event' signaling broader NVIDIA physical AI deployment in Korea beyond HBM deals.

bullets.title: AAPL: Morgan Stanley PT Raised to $360; Apple Intelligence/Siri Narrative Evolving
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley raised its Apple price target to $360 from $330 maintaining Overweight, citing AI monetization potential without heavy capex. Apple's WWDC announcements focused on incremental Siri improvements, macOS 27 performance, and Apple Private Cloud Compute now expanded to Google Cloud using NVIDIA Confidential Computing. Analyst reads: Apple is 'keeping it real' by avoiding moonshot promises.

bullets.title: Sovereign AI Buildout: Nation-States Must Choose US-Stack or China-Stack
bullets.body: A widely-discussed framing emerged: enterprises and nations will be forced onto either the Chinese open-model/Huawei stack or a US government-dependent model/compute access stack. AI export controls signal that companies above certain intelligence thresholds face supply chain risk classification for non-US entities, and model releases are being delayed 3-6+ months. This is seen as bullish for sovereign AI infrastructure spending.

bullets.title: US-Iran Deal Imminent: Strait of Hormuz Reopening Priced In, Then Questioned
bullets.body: Trump announced an Iran peace deal scheduled for Sunday signing with immediate Strait of Hormuz reopening, calling it 'fully negotiated.' Iran's parliament simultaneously rejected the draft and the foreign ministry said no final agreement was reached. Markets whipsawed: oil initially fell 4-5% on ceasefire hope, then rebounded on escalation signals. EIA expects Hormuz oil to resume Q3 2026 but full recovery only in 2027.

bullets.title: SpaceX IPO: 4x Oversubscribed at $1.75T—Retail Funded, Gulf SWFs, ARK Buys
bullets.body: SpaceX raised $75B in the largest IPO in history, reportedly 4x oversubscribed with $250B+ in investor demand. ARK Invest bought $444M on day one, BlackRock put in $5B+, Gulf sovereign wealth funds each bid $1-5B. Stock opened near $165, implying a $2.2T+ market cap. Morningstar warned fair value is $63/share. Leveraged 2x ETFs (SPCH long, SSPC short) launched Monday.

bullets.title: Mag 7 Drawdowns Signal Rotation—Tech Sector Down 10%+ From ATHs
bullets.body: Since S&P 500 ATH on June 2nd, tech fell 10%+ while Healthcare, Staples, REITs, and Financials gained 2%+. Meta and Microsoft are each down 27-28% from all-time highs, PLTR down 36-38%, TSLA down 21-24%. Only 5 of 7 Mag7 stocks have underperformed the S&P 500 YTD, with only GOOGL and NVDA outperforming. Stock-bond correlations hit the most positive level since 1999.

bullets.title: May CPI: Headline 4.2% (In-Line), Core 0.2% Beats; ECB Hikes First Time Since 2023
bullets.body: May US CPI came in at 4.2% YoY (matching estimates) but core CPI beat at 0.2% MoM vs 0.3% expected—driven entirely by a 1.7% MoM car insurance drop. Supercore ran at 5.2% annualized over the March-May period. ECB raised rates 25bps to 2.25% citing energy shock; first hike since 2023. PPI printed 1.1% MoM vs 0.7% estimate, with final demand goods posting largest monthly increase on record (+2.8%).

bullets.title: LITE CEO Confirms CPO Timeline, Calls NPO Opportunity 'Bigger Than CPO'
bullets.body: Lumentum CEO Michael Hurlston confirmed at Needham and Mizuho conferences that the company is on pace to meet or exceed top-end guidance, with scale-up optical products shipping starting H2 2027 and formal ramp in 2028. He stated the NPO opportunity 'is frankly bigger than CPO,' and appeared on two consecutive days at institutional conferences—a bullish signal flagged by fintwit.

bullets.title: Burry Deep-Value Thesis: ADBE at ~11x P/E, PYPL Near Multi-Year Lows
bullets.body: Michael Burry has been building positions in beaten-down names including ADBE (at ~11x P/E, near historical lows) and PYPL (initiated at $49 in April, continuing to add). The thesis: markets punish large, established companies with real earnings and buybacks that don't fit the AI narrative, creating mispricing. RBC cut ADBE PT to $285 from $350.

bullets.title: FOMC Next Week: New Chair, Former Chair Present, Divided Committee—Market Watches
bullets.body: Kevin Warsh runs his first FOMC meeting with Jerome Powell present at the table, described as 'very unusual.' The committee is divided heading into a complex macro backdrop: PPI at 6.5%, CPI at 4.2%, and futures pricing one hike by year-end. Fed futures showed traders paring back hike expectations after the core CPI beat, then repricing on PPI surprise.

bullets.title: SMCI Down 25% on $7B Equity Offering; Warned by Fintwit Ahead of Filing
bullets.body: Super Micro Computer filed for a mixed shelf offering worth approximately 30% of market cap ($7B in equity/equity-linked financing), triggering a 25% intraday decline. The company also disclosed $39B in recent AI server orders, though the source of those orders was questioned. Fintwit accounts had been flagging this risk.

bullets.title: WBD/PSKY Deal: California May Block DOJ Approval
bullets.body: California officials signaled potential opposition to the DOJ-approved PSKY/WBD deal despite federal clearance received the prior day.

bullets.title: AAOI: CFO Conducting Investor Meetings, Street Estimates Below Capacity Plans
bullets.body: Applied Optoelectronics CFO Stefan Murry is actively meeting with institutional investors. Street estimates remain well below the company's capacity plans, suggesting potential for upside earnings revisions. The stock sold off alongside the broader optics sector on SemiAnalysis CPO delay concerns, which fintwit views as overdone.

bullets.title: AMD Dominates Amazon Best-Seller CPU Chart 15-of-15; BofA Double-Upgrades INTC
bullets.body: AMD's marketing chief cited '15 out of 15' top CPU spots on Amazon with Intel holding zero. Separately, Bank of America double-upgraded Intel to Buy from Underperform with a $135 price target, and BofA raised the 2030 server CPU TAM forecast to $170B+ from $125B citing agentic AI demand. AMD also undercuts NVIDIA DGX Spark with Ryzen AI Halo at $3,999 vs. $4,679.

bullets.title: TSMC May Revenue: Record NT$417B (+30% YoY); CoPoS Timeline Advanced to 2028
bullets.body: TSMC reported record May 2026 revenue of NT$417B, up 30.1% YoY and 1.5% MoM, tracking well above FY guidance of >30% growth. Additionally, TSMC advanced its CoPoS advanced packaging technology timeline from 2029 to 2028, a bullish signal for next-gen AI chip packaging supply.
